generated_examples.rule: Each source row becomes one research-only example with the same official URL, fact, gate and confidence. No BNG unit, sewer capacity, parcel relation, allocation or live utility capacity is inferred.

extra_examples.fact: Mandatory BNG generally requires a 10% increase in biodiversity value relative to the pre-development on-site habitat.
extra_examples.gate: Exact exemption status, metric and permission must be checked.

extra_examples.site: England development and off-site gain land
extra_examples.fact: Significant on-site gains and off-site gains must generally be maintained for at least 30 years.
extra_examples.gate: The exact legal agreement/HMMP controls the specific land and obligations.

extra_examples.fact: From 6 August 2026, BNG does not apply to planning applications for developments of 0.2 hectares or below.
extra_examples.gate: Current date is 23 July 2026; do not apply the future exemption early.

extra_examples.fact: BNG becomes mandatory for NSIP DCO applications on or after 2 November 2026.
extra_examples.gate: Do not infer the future statutory rule applies before its commencement date.

extra_examples.ref: LPA eight-week BNG plan decision gate
extra_examples.fact: LPAs must decide whether to approve a Biodiversity Gain Plan within 8 weeks.
extra_examples.gate: A submitted plan is not approved until the actual determination is verified.

extra_examples.fact: LPAs should confirm that off-site gains in the gain plan are registered, allocated to the development and match the biodiversity value on the register.
extra_examples.gate: All three links must be verified for the exact permission before promotion.

extra_examples.fact: The statutory-credit spatial risk multiplier means 2 credits are required for every 1 biodiversity unit shortfall.
extra_examples.gate: Only the exact metric unit shortfall can determine required credits.

extra_examples.fact: The current published hedgerow statutory credit price is £44,000 per credit.
extra_examples.gate: No project cost is inferred without a verified hedgerow shortfall and current price check.

extra_examples.fact: The current published watercourse statutory credit price is £230,000 per credit.
extra_examples.gate: No project cost is inferred without a verified watercourse shortfall and current price check.

extra_examples.fact: Defra reported £426,100 statutory-credit income for 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026.
extra_examples.gate: National credit activity is not parcel demand or viability evidence.

extra_examples.fact: The 2025-26 report says £530,000 was invested in habitat creation/enhancement and 44.6 BNG units were secured through procurement.
extra_examples.gate: National procurement is not an off-site allocation for a specific development.

extra_examples.ref: Planning Data BNG zero-record fail-closed control
extra_examples.fact: The Planning Data BNG-assessment dataset currently has zero records and zero providers.
extra_examples.gate: Zero coverage must never be treated as zero BNG obligations or assessments.

extra_examples.fact: The biodiversity gain sites register can expose a map or plan showing the boundary of a registered gain site.
extra_examples.gate: Register boundary is off-site BNG evidence, not a canonical development parcel boundary.

extra_examples.fact: Where the biodiversity gain condition applies, the Biodiversity Gain Plan must be approved before development starts.
extra_examples.gate: Planning permission alone does not prove the BNG pre-commencement condition has been discharged.

extra_examples.fact: Current statutory guidance expects draft DWMPs by 1 November 2027 for 12-week consultation.
extra_examples.gate: Future draft plans are not current capacity evidence.

extra_examples.fact: Current statutory guidance expects final DWMPs by 31 August 2028.
extra_examples.gate: No future plan output is inferred before publication.

extra_examples.fact: DWMP guidance uses Level 3 sewerage catchments as a core detailed planning level.
extra_examples.gate: Site scoring needs the exact Level 3 catchment and current model, not company-wide context.

extra_examples.fact: United Utilities states its DWMP portal is modelled and does not display live or historic operational information.
extra_examples.gate: Modelled risk cannot be treated as live headroom or a connection confirmation.

extra_examples.fact: Anglian Water says its displayed risk-based catchment screening is based on the 2019 exercise, despite annual review.
extra_examples.gate: Historic screening cannot be treated as current wastewater capacity.

extra_examples.ref: Thames DWMP28 scope: population and climate
extra_examples.fact: Thames Water's current DWMP28 scope explicitly includes population change, climate change, asset health and new regulatory requirements.
extra_examples.gate: Scope identifies drivers, not a specific development's capacity position.

extra_examples.fact: Southern Water's statutory DWMP uses wastewater-system boundaries as its most local reporting geography alongside region and river-basin levels.
extra_examples.gate: Exact development must be matched to the relevant wastewater system before capacity analysis.

extra_examples.ref: Adur and Ouse overflow/flood priority example
extra_examples.fact: Southern Water identifies overflow and sewer-flooding reduction priorities around locations including Lewes and Shoreham in the Adur and Ouse catchment.
extra_examples.gate: Catchment priority is not a live connection constraint for a parcel.

extra_examples.fact: Southern Water identifies overflow/flood-risk priorities around Kennington and Westbere in the Stour catchment.
extra_examples.gate: Exact wastewater system and current model are still required.

extra_examples.fact: Southern Water identifies wastewater/flood priorities around locations including Motney Hill, Ticehurst, Hildenborough, Penshurst and Gravesend.
extra_examples.gate: Catchment context is not a connection approval or exact capacity measurement.
